claims.body: The Predators kill penalties well, but the Islanders don’t. Nashville is near the top of the league for the penalty kill, and the Islanders are one of the worst. Penalties should hurt the Islanders more than the Predators.

notes.text: Kyle Palmieri is no longer killing penalties: 0% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, down from 37% last season.

They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Ross Colton takes shifts on two lines, L2 and L4. Daemon Hunt is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Perbix and Hague.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 26% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 6th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 44%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Adam Edström has started killing penalties: on the ice for 28% of the team’s shorthanded time in 11 games, up from 1% with his old team last season.

stakes: The Islanders go in tied for fourth in the Metropolitan with 12 points, the Predators fifth in the Central with 12 points.

NSH.head: Leaning the Predators’ way
NSH.body: The Islanders have been out-chancing opponents lately, but Nashville has home-ice advantage. Still, it’s close: the Islanders can make it interesting if they keep shots to a minimum.

NYI.head: A slightly uphill night for the Islanders
NYI.body: The Islanders have been out-chancing opponents lately, but Nashville has home-ice advantage. The Islanders’ best way to tip it is keeping shots to a minimum.
